title: Theoretical and applied psychology of communication
abstract: Context and relevance. The year 2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the birth of the renowned Russian psychologist, philologist, and educator Alexei Alekseevich Leontiev (1936-2004). In keeping with established scientific tradition, events dedicated to this anniversary celebrate the scientist's ideas through the lens of the current state of science and practice. Publications aimed at drawing attention to the scientist's legacy occupy a prominent place among these scientific events. This article discusses the collection of scientific papers “Psychology of Communication” (Moscow: Smysl, 2026), published for the anniversary and addressed to a wide range of readers in the humanities. Objective is to briefly introduce the works of A.A. Leontiev included in this collection, as well as to explore the rationale for collecting these works under one cover and presenting them as a coherent whole. Hypothesis. An analysis of A.A. Leontiev's scientific legacy in the field of communication studies provides grounds for considering the results of his research from various perspectives—linguistic, psychological, and pedagogical—as reflected in relevant publications. Methods and materials. The method used was a historical and methodological analysis of A.A. Leontiev's works based on the publications included in the publication under review. Results. The evolution of communication research is demonstrated, and the logic of the author's scientific research is traced, beginning with works in the field of psycholinguistics and ending with general publications on the psychology of communication, which suggest the possibility of applying an activity-based approach to communication processes. Conclusions. An analysis of A.A. Leontiev's research on communication issues demonstrates the development of an original, interdisciplinary approach to the study of communication.
